newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group warns of imminent rival attack.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group warns of imminent rival attack.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group said on Wednesday a rival militia group and Iraqi forces had built up forces in northern Iraq over the last few days in an indication of a possible attack.

The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) said there were signs of an imminent attack by the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) of Massoud Barzani and the troops of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein on the PUK stronghold, Sulaimaniya province.
"The building-up of Saddam-Barzani troops during the past few days and the closure of the main roads in the area are clear signs of an imminent attack," the PUK statement said.
"There is nothing new. I do not believe there is any basis for these accusations," a KDP spokesman told Reuters.
The rival KDP and PUK have held several rounds of talks in Ankara aimed at forging a permanent peace in northern Iraq following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire last October.
The PUK statement called on the United States, Britain and Turkey, brokers at the Ankara talks, to prevent any attack.
At the end of August the KDP joined with Iraqi troops to wrest control of Arbil, northern Iraq's administrative centre, from the PUK.
The clashes gave Baghdad a foothold in the region for the first time since the end of the Gulf War in 1991 and prompted retaliatory U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
